candidate.selection_reason: Unvalidated property key -> isSafeProperty check -> prevents unsafe property access
candidate.source_summary: Property keys come from user input via expression parsing - keys can be symbols or quoted strings from math expressions like {toString: 1} or {"constructor": 2}
candidate.sink_summary: Keys are used in JavaScript code generation via compile() function, potentially allowing prototype pollution if unsafe properties like 'constructor' or 'toString' are allowed
candidate.guard_summary: isSafeProperty check blocks properties that exist on empty object prototype (constructor, toString, valueOf, etc.) - present and effective on the demonstrated path
candidate.risk_pattern: User-controlled object property keys in expression compilation could access dangerous prototype properties if not validated, enabling prototype pollution attacks
candidate.context_summary: Security check added to prevent unsafe property access during JavaScript code compilation from math expressions
unresolved_facts: Complete list of properties blocked by isSafeProperty
Specific attack scenarios beyond prototype pollution
Whether other ObjectNode methods need similar protection

target_cwe.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
target_cwe.description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output that is used as a web page that is served to other users.
remediation_steps: Use parameterized queries and prepared statements
Implement strict input validation with whitelisting

stage3_hypothesis.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
stage3_hypothesis.fit_reason: Prototype pollution can escalate to XSS via modification of prototype methods used in code generation
